ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, senior officers and beneficial owners against: FIC targeted financial sanctions lists maintained under POCDATARA; UN Security Council consolidated list; OFAC SDN list (secondary compliance due to Swift_LC and TT_Wire USD clearing); UK HM Treasury consolidated list; and EU CFSP consolidated list. Enhanced Due Diligence under FICA s.21E applies to foreign and domestic prominent PEPs, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Given the High_Risk_Special_License AgTech drone profile, negative-news screening and dual-use export-control exposure checks against the NCACC controlled-goods watchlist are mandatory before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal, CoR 9.1 online name-reservation module (b-reserved)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in a readable Latin (A-Z) transliteration; CIPC accepts names in any of the eleven South African official languages but English and Afrikaans are preferable to minimise search-conflict refusals; a foreign-script name must be certified-transliterated into Latin characters by a sworn translator; the full statutory name must include 'Proprietary Limited' or the accepted abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank / banc / banker (prior South African Reserve Bank consent)
building society / mutual / provident (Prudential Authority consent)
insurance / assurance / underwriter (Prudential Authority and FSCA consent)
financial services / lender / credit provider (FSCA licence condition)
stock exchange / derivatives exchange (FSCA licence condition)
national / government / RSA / state (false state-affiliation bar)
defence / armaments / military / munitions (NCACC classification; dual-use drone token triggers defence export-control screening)
cooperative / co-op (exclusively reserved for Co-operatives Act 14 of 2005 entities)
offensive, obscene or scandalous expressions (s.11(2)(c) absolute bar)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC rejection under s.11(2) Companies Act 71 of 2008, the applicant may file a reconsideration request via CIPC e-Services using additional search tokens within the unexpired reservation window. If rejection is sustained, a fresh CoR 9.1 may be lodged with alternative names at the statutory fee. For formal adjudication, an aggrieved applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under s.160 within 10 business days of the refusal notice; an unsuccessful Tribunal outcome may be taken on judicial review to the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 within 180 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted: a serviced-office or managed virtual-office arrangement is acceptable provided it maintains a physical street address in South Africa (no post-box only), has a manned reception or document-acceptance agent, and is capable of receiving SARS and CIPC statutory process. Fully cloud-based 'shadow' addresses without any physical South African presence will be rejected by banks during FICA account-opening and may invalidate the s.23 Companies Act registered-office obligation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office (serviced node): 8-15% annualised risk of unannounced physical inspection or service of process. Manufacturing and storage premises: 45-55% once VAT, customs and SARS income-tax registrations are active, with SARS audit teams conducting unannounced asset and inventory verification relevant to drone production and export records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended, ss 1, 11, 13, 14, 15, 19, and 66; Companies Regulations 2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement. A private company must issue at least one share upon incorporation; share consideration is determined by the directors and this will form part of the first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers having accepted the memorandum and articles of association and the registered office having been established, the directors appointed on incorporation hereby resolve: (1) the allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares to the founding subscribers at par, fully paid from contributions received; (2) adoption of the registered office and the appointment of the company secretary and first auditor; (3) ratification of the incorporation filings lodged with CIPC; and (4) authorisation of the directors to open banking accounts, apply for sectoral licences, and execute all ancillary instruments. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be minuted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and company structure confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC eServices, select company registration, and either reserve the proposed company name through CoR 9.1 or confirm on the CoR 14.1 that no name reservation is requested. Confirm the private company (Pty) Ltd structure, authorised share classes, and first directors. Download the draft MOI and internal constitution for director approval.
required_dossiers: Certified ID or passport copies of incorporators
Proposed company name details or reserved name proof
Directors' personal details and consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, file an alternative name or objection with CIPC within the statutory period; the incorporators may proceed with a distinguishable alternative name without losing the benefit of the initial filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of CoR 14.1, MOI, and director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices or accredited company registration practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and attach the signed MOI, which must comply with the Companies Act for a private company. State the financial year end, share capital, directors, and registered address. Foreign incorporators must provide notarially certified copies and apostilled identity documents. Ensure director consents are signed and dated.
required_dossiers: Identity or passport copies of all directors
Proof of registered office domicile (municipal statement or lease)
Apostilled/notarised documents for non-South African signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query, amend and resubmit the CoR 14.1 and MOI through the same CIPC eServices case within 30 days. Pay any incremental filing fee only if CIPC confirms the amendment is chargeable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission, payment, and issuance of registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed filing package, pay the prescribed CIPC registration fee using the South African banking payment method integrated in eServices, and retain the payment reference. Monitor the case progress in the eServices dashboard until the company registration number is assigned.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment fails or the case is rejected, reinitiate payment and resubmit through the CIPC payment gateway; use the CIPC eSupport ticket system to reconcile any duplicated payment or case error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Download of Certificate of Incorporation and company extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once CIPC approves the incorporation, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the company extract. Verify that the company name, registration number, incorporation date, registered address, and directors are correct. Obtain a CIPC company record before proceeding to tax and banking registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the SLA, escalate through the CIPC contact centre or e-services dispute desk. Request a letter of authority or company extract to facilitate parallel registrations with SARS and banks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compulsory tax and employment registration (SARS and Department of Employment and Labour)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SARS eFiling; Compensation Fund and Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax on SARS eFiling using the CIPC registration number. Apply for VAT, PAYE, UIF, and SDL if registration thresholds or employer obligations apply. Register as an employer with the Compensation Fund for COIDA and obtain the Letter of Good Standing where required for tenders or licensing.
required_dossiers: Proof of bank account or banking details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or queries the registration, use eFiling to file a corrigendum with the correct entity information. For COIDA/Compensation Fund issues, contact the Department of Employment and Labour's registration desk and resubmit the taxpayer and CIPC supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and share capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FIC Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach an authorised commercial bank in South Africa and complete FICA due diligence. Provide the certified corporate documents, beneficial ownership schedule, and first board resolution. Pay initial share subscription funds into the corporate account if required by the MOI and obtain proof of deposit for the accountant's verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and CIPC company extract
First board resolution authorising account opening
Certified IDs of directors and beneficial owners
Beneficial ownership register / CIPC BOR schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries FICA documents, promptly provide apostilled and certified copies of the corporate resolutions and the CIPC beneficial ownership submission. Resubmit the corrected KYC pack and request a written bank decision within the bank's prescribed review period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) through Invest SA; South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) for aeronautical product and manufacturing approvals; International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC) for import/export controls
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: SACAA Production Organisation Approval / Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems Manufacturing Approval, together with an ITAC export/import permit for controlled or dual-use goods where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under the NEMA EIA Regulations for light industrial manufacturing in an existing industrial zone; Full Scoping and Environmental Impact Reporting if Listing Notice 2 activities, hazardous waste, or significant atmospheric emissions are triggered; otherwise a registration or exemption may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004, for VOC, particulate, and hazardous air pollutant thresholds; obtain an Atmospheric Emission Licence if the facility exceeds Minimum Emission Standards; apply for water use licensing under the National Water Act, 1998, for industrial effluent discharge; handle and dispose of electronic, battery, and solvent waste under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008, and adhere to municipal trade effluent and noise by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local municipal fire protection authority; structural load stability and electrical certificate of compliance from a registered municipal building inspector; Certificate of Occupancy; Department of Employment and Labour factory registration and COIDA clearance; Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993, workplace compliance including ventilation, hazardous chemical storage, and electrostatic discharge controls for UAV assembly and battery stores.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – national tax and customs administration; taxpayer portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); corporate registry interface: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC, https://www.cipc.co.za).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with CIPC (Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation) to obtain the CIPC registration number. 2. Appoint a public officer resident in South Africa within one month of incorporation (s 246 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011). 3. Register the company with SARS through eFiling or a SARS branch to obtain the Income Tax Reference Number (ITRN), using the CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, public officer identity document, and beneficial-ownership records. 4. File a VAT 101 application for VAT vendor registration: compulsory within 21 days of exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 taxable supplies in a 12-month period; voluntary from ZAR 50,000 (recommended for export manufacturers to recover input VAT). 5. If employees are appointed, register for PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy before the first remuneration payment via eFiling. 6. Register with SARS Customs for a Customs Client Code (importer/exporter code) and complete the electronic RCG-02 customs registration to enable outward declarations. 7. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of issued shares without a local shareholder, but the public officer must be resident in South Africa. The resulting statutory tax identity comprises the ITRN, the VAT vendor number (where registered), and the Customs Client Code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a South African-resident (Pty) Ltd is subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income at the standard rate of 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; no pass-through or check-the-box eligibility. Distributions to shareholders attract dividend withholding tax at 20% (subject to applicable treaty relief). Foreign holding structures are subject to controlled foreign company rules under s 9D of the Income Tax Act; South Africa does not offer a territorial exemption or automatic export-zone status for this manufacturing activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Domestic (Pty) Ltd classification follows the CIPC legal form and is not elective. Available elections: (i) group taxation election under s 41(1) Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, available to a resident holding company controlling at least 75% of a subsidiary, permitting intra-group loss offset and asset-transfer rollover; (ii) VAT group vendor application under s 50 VAT Act 89 of 1991, allowing connected companies to share a single VAT registration number; (iii) s 11D research-and-development tax incentive election, granting a 10% incremental allowance for qualifying agri-tech R&D performed in South Africa; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules effective 1 January 2024 – no check-the-box election exists, but a participant in a hybrid entity (for example a US LLC or foreign trust) must apply the s 1(1) definition, report the arrangement through the Reportable Arrangement/INR process, and make mandatory deduction/non-inclusion adjustments; (v) the former s 9E headquarter-company election was repealed with effect from 1 January 2021 and is no longer available.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961. Day-to-day administration is delegated to Authorized Dealers (South African commercial banks licensed for foreign exchange) under FinSurv directives, with technical oversight of the National Payment System Department for clearing rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current-account trade and service transactions, with documentation-based reporting through the SARS/SARB electronic filing systems. The capital account remains restricted: direct inbound equity and shareholder loans from non-residents are permitted without prior FinSurv approval when routed through an Authorized Dealer, but outbound capital transfers, foreign borrowings exceeding the local financial assistance (LFA) formula, outward direct investment, and cross-border guarantees require prior approval or a specific dispensation. Profit repatriation is lawful via declared dividends to non-resident shareholders provided the shares were acquired with inward funds introduced through the banking system and the 'loop structure' prohibition (South African-resident funds indirectly used to acquire the local investment) is not breached. Dividend remittances are subject to 20% Dividends Tax unless reduced under an applicable double-tax agreement; royalties and service fees are transferable at arm's length with valid SARS tax clearance or withholding certificates. Practical convertibility is high for a compliant exporter; the binding constraints are documentary discipline, the LFA borrowing envelope, and FinSurv reporting rather than availability of foreign exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory surrender of export proceeds to ZAR has been abolished. However, exporters must repatriate export proceeds to South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment, or within a FinSurv-approved extended period. Proceeds must be received through an Authorized Dealer and electronically declared via the SARS/SARB Export Management System (EMS). The exporter may retain up to 100% of realized export proceeds in a designated Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorized Dealer, and there is no statutory minimum conversion into ZAR; FCA balances may fund import payments, trade settlements, and working capital. Open-account exports above ZAR 50 million per transaction, or credit terms beyond 180 days, require FinSurv scrutiny or approval. Full export documentation (bill of lading, invoice, proof of receipt, EMS reference) must be archived for at least five years, and non-repatriation constitutes an exchange-control offense.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR) + Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR) + Trade Finance Line (LC issuance/confirmation). Inward non-resident capital funds are credited to a designated capital-escrowed operational sub-account and classified under an EM code for onward profit-repatriation tracking.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank - FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR) + FCA (USD/EUR) with integrated online FX dealing; parallel Capital Escrow Account functionality for locked inward share-capital funds pending CIPC filings and issuance of share certificates.

Operational Account (ZAR) + single FCA (USD/EUR); suitable for holding export proceeds under the 180-day rule, executing SWIFT MT103 settlements, and supporting documentary credit facilities for drone exports.
Operational Account (ZAR) + FCA (USD/EUR); strong agricultural trade desk and SADC/SACU documentary credit capabilities, with dedicated agro-industrial relationship management.
Specialized private-bank tier Account (ZAR operational + FCA) with tailored FX advisory and trade structuring; requires higher relationship thresholds and minimum balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. South Africa has no European-style EMI passport; non-bank payment service providers require a National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 license and PASA membership, and offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) cannot lawfully hold ZAR corporate balances, issue local clearing codes, or execute trade settlements and export-proceeds repatriation on behalf of the company. Offshore EMIs may be engaged only as auxiliary channels for low-value disbursements, funded from an onshore bank account; the main treasury, LC, export-proceeds, FX-hedging, and FinSurv reporting flows must sit with a regulated South African Authorized Dealer. Feasibility rating: Medium as auxiliary platform, Low as primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated under FICA where independent electronic verification is possible; however, in practice, a high-risk, non-resident-owned manufacturing entity will be required to present its lead director and signatories for an in-person or live-video onboarding interview with the relationship banker at the branch. Foreign directors must supply original passports, apostilled or notarized proof of residential address, and a board resolution appointing signatories; documents certified by a South African commissioner of oaths are accepted for remote filing. The company must hold a valid SARS income-tax registration (plus VAT and customs code where applicable), a CIPC-registered Memorandum of Incorporation for the (Pty) Ltd structure, and a registered physical business address in South Africa. Remote opening is possible for the initial compliance file at the banker's discretion, but the practical standard requires at least one local representative or duly authorized director to complete the interview in Johannesburg, Cape Town, or Durban before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tier-1 AML risk profiling: the entity manufactures autonomous UAV crop sprayers categorized as dual-use technology under the bank's sectoral policy, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential diversion-to-military-use concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive technical and legal package: (i) ITAC import/export permit with end-use declaration; (ii) SACAA/RPAS registration (if applicable) and certificate confirming agricultural-only operating scope; (iii) product specification sheet demonstrating sprayer payload, flow rates, and non-weaponizable design; (iv) end-user certificate and resale-restriction undertaking from each foreign buyer; (v) internal export compliance policy and denied-party screening log; (vi) serial-number tracking and inventory records; (vii) third-party technology audit confirming absence of ITAR/EU dual-use controlled components.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership: non-resident parent/shareholder chain without clear source of wealth, triggering 'shell risk' and potential reverse-money-laundering flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO declaration on FICA forms; CIPC company extraction; certified shareholders register and share certificates; group organization chart; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds certificates issued by the foreign bank; three years of audited financial statements of the parent; PEP screening results; and a sworn affidavit describing the economic purpose of the South African entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident equity injections and intercompany loans creating transaction velocity inconsistent with the agri-drone business plan, raising suspicion of pass-through or unlawful capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan and share-subscription agreements with commercial terms; board-approved treasury policy and capital plan; Authorized Dealer EM classification codes evidencing inward non-resident capital; proof of manufactured and exported goods (bills of lading and EMS declarations); commercial invoices and packing lists; local payroll and operating-expense ledger; tax returns and transfer-pricing documentation aligned with OECD principles and Section 31 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic exposure to buyers in jurisdictions with perceived high money-laundering and financing-of-terrorism risk, generating suspicious-transaction indicators in procurement and settlement patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tiered counterparty due-diligence file per buyer: business registration extract, beneficial-owner declaration, bank account confirmation issued by the buyer's bank, end-use undertaking, sanctions/PEP screening certificate, prior trade references, and a watch-list vetting log; payment-rail discipline restricting settlements to bank transfers against invoices; retained correspondence with freight forwarders; and a documented escalation matrix for any payment deviation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans must be introduced via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident parent or investor through an Authorized Dealer, using the appropriate ISO 20022 transaction purpose code for inward direct investment (BOP equity classification) with reference fields stating 'Non-resident share subscription - [company name]' or 'Intra-group shareholder loan - [loan agreement reference]'. Funds are credited and immediately classified by the Authorized Dealer as inward non-resident capital, which anchors the future right to remit dividends and loan repayments; the Authorized Dealer records the EM classification and notifies FinSurv where the transaction exceeds delegated thresholds. Employment of funds for working capital is unrestricted, provided share certificates or capital increases and the loan agreement are executed promptly. The company must retain the original SWIFT confirmation, loan agreement, board resolution, and the Authorized Dealer's classification record in its compliance file for the full period during which repatriation rights are exercised.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Export trade settlements are executed through Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) confirmed by the South African Authorized Dealer for high-value drone consignments to non-SACU buyers; smaller SADC-regional transactions settle via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer or documentary collections (DP/DA). Imported components (engines, electronics, spray systems) are paid by MT103 against invoices or by import LC where supplier financing is required. The FCA (USD/EUR) serves as the natural funding reserve for outbound payments and must be managed within the 180-day export-receipt rule. All outbound payments require underlying documentation (invoice, bill of lading, airway bill, packing list); payments to related parties must conform to transfer-pricing documentation under Section 31 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and be accompanied by the relevant SARS tax clearance certificates. For LC and documentary-collection business, the bank's trade desk generally requires pre-approved facility limits and compliant shipping documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) concluded with an Authorized Dealer for a firm trade receivable or payable, typically up to 12 months, extendable at dealer discretion upon verification of the underlying commercial exposure.

ZAR Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) executed through an Authorized Dealer where physical ZAR settlement is operationally constrained; SARB's 2021 reforms permit Authorized Dealers to transact NDFs with offshore counterparties for genuine underlying exposure.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) or FX Swap with an Authorized Dealer for longer-dated USD-ZAR capital or investment exposure, subject to FinSurv notification or approval where notional and maturity exceed standard trade-book limits.
Currency Option (USD-ZAR put/call) written by an Authorized Dealer for genuine commercial exposure, with premium settled onshore and no speculative-leverage construction.

Zero-Cost Collar structures (purchased put plus sold call) permissible for trade-backed cash-flow hedging, provided the package is documented as a risk-management instrument and not a speculative trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company is immediately deemed to be in default; CIPC may issue a compliance notice and late-filing penalties accrue. Continued non-compliance enables CIPC to commence involuntary deregistration (administrative strike-off) under section 82(1)(b) after final notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register confirmation and ownership-change notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual return; each share transfer or beneficial-ownership change must be filed within 30 business days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an ownership-change notice is a statutory offence; the company and each director may be subject to administrative penalties and criminal liability, and the company remains in CIPC default until compliant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to public and state-owned companies and to any company whose Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more. A private company with a PIS between 100 and 349 must have an independent review; a PIS below 100 triggers no statutory audit or review unless the Memorandum of Incorporation requires otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for public and accountable companies; IFRS for SMEs for private companies with a PIS below 350; GRAP for public-sector entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 2022, the company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and confirm its accuracy to CIPC with each annual return. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed as a prescribed notice within 30 business days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D research and development super-deduction of 150%; Section 12C accelerated capital allowance of 40/20/20/20 on qualifying manufacturing plant; Section 12B 100% first-year renewable energy allowance; Section 12I industrial project investment and training allowances; 15% preferential corporate income tax rate for qualifying operations in approved Special Economic Zones.
corporate_income_tax_regime.assessed_loss_regime: Unlimited carryforward of assessed losses; from 1 April 2022, annual set-off is restricted to the greater of ZAR 1 million or 80% of taxable income before loss set-off.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 - Income Tax Return for Companies, filed electronically through the SARS eFiling portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be submitted within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year of assessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, SARS tax reference number, CIPC registration number, trade classification (ISIC), and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The proprietary limited entity is a South African tax resident by incorporation; non-resident shareholder details are disclosed in the connected-person schedule, not as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting standards applied (IFRS or SA GAAP), functional currency, and attached financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-parent branch filing ITR14 should state whether foreign-currency statements are used and translate taxable income to ZAR at the year-end ruling exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from agricultural drone sales, maintenance, software services, and export receipts, including Swift LC and TT Wire settlement amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch taxpayers must report only South African-source gross income; profits from offshore manufacturing not attributable to the SA branch should be excluded under the applicable double tax treaty business-profits article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Cost of sales and deductible expenditure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, manufacturing and payroll costs, R&D expenses, royalties, interest, and other deductions allowable under Section 11(a) and related provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses actually incurred in the production of South African income; head-office charges to a branch are deductible only where they are real and arm's-length, supported by documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for cross-border connected-person transactions, showing arm's-length consideration and any payments for IP, loans, or services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related-party transactions must be benchmarked under an approved OECD methodology; failure to disclose or substantiate triggers SARS recharacterisation and understatement penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Assessed loss brought forward / set-off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed loss utilized in the current period and any current-year assessed loss to be carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only a South African branch's own assessed losses may be carried forward; foreign head-office losses are not available, and a change in ownership over 50% may forfeit losses under Section 20A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable income and normal tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after loss set-off and normal tax at 27%, or at the 15% SEZ rate if qualifying and approved.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branches of foreign companies pay normal tax at 27% on SA-source business income; no additional branch remittance tax is charged, but dividend, interest, and royalty withholding taxes apply separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Taxes paid, provisional credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRP6 provisional tax credits, PAYE withheld, foreign tax credits under Section 6quat, and any dividend withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not utilise the South African subsidiary's tax credits on their own returns; foreign tax credits for branch taxes may be claimed under the relevant tax treaty and Section 6quat.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-submission triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty of up to ZAR 250 per day per return event, with caps of approximately ZAR 16,000 per month; SARS may issue an estimated assessment, add 10%-150% understatement penalties, and impose interest on the shortfall.
